title: Telemetry-led environment replay harness for private/VPC benchmarking
creator: Evan Lee
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible, telemetry-driven load harness that can replay realistic customer VPC/on-prem traffic against Private deployments and produce deterministic metrics (tokens/sec, p95 latency, kv-cache hit, GPU utilization) for regression detection.

Scope:
- Capture minimal, privacy-preserving telemetry snapshots from a live customer run (prefix distribution, request sizes, sequence length histogram, model variant, routing decisions).
- Convert telemetry to an executable workload profile that drives our load generator (deterministic RNG seeds, request timing distribution, client-side KV cache priming).
- Support topology emulation (VIPs, NLB latency knobs, inter-shard network delays) and operator-configurable network fault injection.
- Instrument and export standardized metrics: tokens_per_sec, p95_latency_ms, p50_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, stall_rate, gpu_util_pct, per_shard_queue_len, token_emit_variance.
- Regression detection: compute baseline windows, apply EWMA + CUSUM and bootstrap confidence intervals to flag sustained drops in tokens/sec or p95 regressions.
- Produce reproducible run artifacts: workload.json, seed.txt, snapshot.tar.gz and deterministic run UUID.

Design decisions:
- Determinism: Use fixed RNG seed written to seed.txt and include environment fingerprint (model_version, runtime-kernel-hash, sequence_length_bucketing) so runs are attributable. This avoids non-determinism from ephemeral scheduling.
- Privacy: Telemetry snapshots redacted; only aggregate distributions (histograms) and non-PHI identifiers stored. Any raw prompts are hashed with customer salt and discarded.
- Cache priming: Harness supports pre-warm phase that replays prefix set to populate KV cache to realistic hit rates before measurement window.
- Metrics cadence: 10s buckets exported to Grafana; p95 computed client-side and server-side to catch client-observed vs infra latency drifts.
- Regression algorithm: baseline uses last 5 stable runs (rolling window), we compute a paired test and CUSUM for change point detection. Alerts triggered when tokens/sec falls > 15% below baseline sustained for 3 windows and p95 increases > 30% with p<0.01.

Artifacts & integrations:
- Load generator: bench-driver (Go) with gRPC + HTTP modes, supports rate-limited token-streaming and function call emulation.
- Storage: reproducible runs uploaded to s3://redwood-private-bench/runs/<run-id>/ with logs, metrics.json, workload.json.
- Dashboards: Grafana dashboards under team:benchmarks (link below).
- PRs and design docs linked in comments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Run reproduces a customer VPC snapshot end-to-end in our staging private cluster and yields <=5% variance on tokens/sec across 3 deterministic runs when runtime binary unchanged.
- Regression detection marks a synthetic regression (we will inject a kernel slowdown) and creates an alert with run artifact link and suggested rollback tag.
- Security review completed and telemetry redaction validated by compliance.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Evan Lee: RFC posted to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PI/Telemetry+Replay+Harness). Seeking feedback from infra, runtime, and security. Main ask: can we capture enough from customer runs to synthesize realistic inter-request spacing without storing raw prompts?

2026-02-20 - Marco Rivera (runtime): Reviewed design; asked to include runtime-kernel-hash in fingerprinting and clarified that GPU context switching non-determinism will be a known source of variance. Suggested adding a 'kernel-pin' toggle to the harness to enforce pinned kernels for determinism tests.

2026-02-22 - Sofia Patel (security): Confirmed redaction approach acceptable if raw prompt text is not stored and hashes are one-way with per-customer salts. Requested KMS-backed salt rotation for archived runs older than 90 days. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-02-25 - Aisha Khan: Initial prototype bench-driver v0.1 pushed (https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-driver/pull/118). Prototype supports workload.json generation from telemetry histograms, deterministic RNG, and a cache pre-warm phase. Manual run against staging produced metrics.json and upload to s3.

2026-02-27 - QA: Repro run 2026-02-27T14:12 showed tokens_per_sec variance ~12% across three runs; investigation points to network jitter in staging and one worker with stale kernel. Added 'network-stable' pre-check to operator CLI that verifies network p95 jitter < 3ms before measurement window.

2026-03-01 - Aisha Khan: Implemented CUSUM-based regression detector and bootstrap confidence intervals. Hooked alerts to #benchmarks-alerts Slack channel and created a run-template that includes instructions for attaching a reproducer PR.
